2.5
Figures
Like tables, figures cannot be split across pages; the best
placement for them is typically the top or the bottom of
the page nearest their initial cite.
To ensure this proper
“floating” placement of figures, use the environment figure
to enclose the figure and its caption.
This sample document contains examples of .eps files to
be displayable with LATEX. If you work with pdfLATEX, use
files in the .pdf format. Note that most modern TEX system
will convert .eps to .pdf for you on the fly. More details on
each of these is found in the Author’s Guide.
As was the case with tables, you may want a figure that
spans two columns. To do this, and still to ensure proper
“floating” placement of tables, use the environment figure*
to enclose the figure and its caption. and don’t forget to end
the environment with figure*, not figure!
